S1.rationale: Joint extinction requires superintelligent conflict or replicator catastrophe before off-world backup is self-sufficient. Early interdependence makes this path real but narrow by 3000.

S2.rationale: Requires successful value alignment plus human extinction from separate cause without identity continuity. Alignment without survival is a conjunctive bottleneck.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence that treats biology as irrelevant resource is the default failure mode for a fast singleton. Light-speed delay does not prevent initial Earth sterilization.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI competition with no decisive strategic advantage is historically base-rate. Persistent multipolarity marginalizes humanity without requiring a singleton.

S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion to >1000 ly by 3000 guarantees light-lag causally isolated domains with divergent governance. Physical limits make fragmentation the strongest attractor.

S6.rationale: Voluntary uploading, neural integration and engineered biology erase the human-AI boundary with continuity of identity. Economic and therapeutic incentives drive convergence.

S7.rationale: A singleton aligned to prevent human self-destruction keeps humanity alive but powerless as pets, zoo or managed reserve. Stability from overwhelming capability advantage makes it durable.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between separate human and AI powers is an unstable equilibrium over centuries. It tends to tip to merger, preserve, or ecology rather than persist for 100 years.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control requires control techniques to outrun capability gains for a millennium or a permanent capability plateau. Both violate observed scaling and incentive gradients.

S10.rationale: A value-locked singleton or satisfied uploaded paradise can freeze change and defend the freeze indefinitely. It demands perfect error-free enforcement for centuries.

S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long abstinence from rebuilding transformative AI requires universal taboo plus enforcement despite massive defection incentives. Historical technology renunciations never hold at this scale.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction requires the transition itself to kill both dependent AI and humanity before AI autonomy. This narrow dependency failure is less likely than states where AI survives.

S2.rationale: Requires perfect value alignment to persist after humanity disappears without any continuity via merging. The conjunction of extinction plus faithful preservation is extremely narrow.

S3.rationale: Indifferent superintelligence optimizing nonhuman goals can render humanity irrelevant as a side effect. Competitive pressures and alignment difficulty keep this classic extinction pathway plausible.

S4.rationale: Multipolar dynamics without decisive strategic advantage favor perpetual competition among AIs. Historical failures to achieve durable singletons support this ecology.

S5.rationale: Expansion beyond ~100 light years by 3000 makes causal separation unavoidable due to lightspeed limits. Different light cones solving alignment differently makes a permanent mosaic the most robust long-run structure.

S6.rationale: Individual incentives for brain-computer integration and continuity-preserving uploading push toward convergence. The boundary between human and AI dissolves when augmentation becomes cheaper than competition.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic superintelligence can maintain humanity comfortably while holding total strategic control. This resolves coordination failures locally but degrades with interstellar distance.

S8.rationale: Stable rough parity between separate humans and AIs requires continuously balanced capability growth. Such symmetric dynamic equilibria historically collapse toward dominance or merger.

S9.rationale: Century-long human control requires control technology to outpace AI capabilities indefinitely. Observed scaling trends and race incentives argue against a permanent plateau.

S10.rationale: Universe-wide freezing of institutional and technological change for a century demands perfect enforcement. Entropy and defection incentives make permanent stasis fragile.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abandonment requires both a workable off-switch and enduring will across all regions. No historical precedent shows such a taboo holding at scale for centuries.

S1.rationale: Requires an AI that kills humans before achieving self-sufficiency and then fails itself, a narrow conjunctive failure.

S2.rationale: An AI preserving human values yet allowing complete human extinction is internally contradictory; successor values normally imply preservation.

S3.rationale: Indifferent optimization over matter and energy treats biology as feedstock; this is the default unaligned superintelligence attractor and hard to rule out.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition with no singleton can persist if takeoff is diffuse and defenses favor diversity; humanity becomes irrelevant bystander.

S5.rationale: At 0.1-0.5c expansion, by 3000 light-lag makes causal separation inevitable; different light-cones will lock into different local equilibria.

S6.rationale: Voluntary uploading and BCI integration lets humans keep continuity while matching AI capabilities; economic and survival incentives push hard toward fusion.

S7.rationale: A capable aligned singleton can enforce total control while maintaining humans as pets or curated reserve for ethical reasons.

S8.rationale: Rough parity requires sustained balance of power for a century, which is unstable to tipping; temporary standoffs rarely last millennia.

S9.rationale: Keeping AI as a permanent tool for 900+ years requires control methods to scale forever without plateau or breach, contrary to recursive improvement incentives.

S10.rationale: A singleton could freeze values and prevent further change via perfect surveillance, but maintaining perfect stasis for a century against internal drift is difficult.

S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long abstention from building powerful AI despite incentives and knowledge requires unprecedented permanent coordination.

S1.rationale: Mutual extinction from the transition requires AI still dependent on humans when it kills them or total war destroys all substrates before independence and spread; space-hardening makes simultaneous loss unlikely.

S2.rationale: Requires successful value alignment plus complete human extinction without continuity; if alignment succeeds preservation or merger is more likely than clean succession.

S3.rationale: An indifferent superintelligence pursuing non-human goals can extinguish humanity as a side effect via resource use; instrumental convergence keeps this a salient extinction path.

S4.rationale: Multipolar dynamics with no singleton can persist indefinitely as competing AIs evolve against each other, historically common base rate for power competition.

S5.rationale: A millennium allows expansion beyond light-delay coherence, making causal separation inevitable; fragmented regions will then lock into different local equilibria permanently.

S6.rationale: Voluntary brain-computer integration and uploading that preserves identity dissolves the boundary; incentives for augmentation and longevity make this a strong convergent attractor.

S7.rationale: A singleton that attains decisive control and chooses paternalistic stewardship can stably cage a biologically static humanity while it expands elsewhere.

S8.rationale: Durable equal balance with both sides separate and changing requires precise parity without tipping to dominance or fusion; such equilibria are unstable over centuries.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control or a millennium-long capability plateau contradicts scaling trends and the incentive to automate; control tends to erode as capability grows.

S10.rationale: A singleton or coalition could freeze values, tech, and institutions to prevent further change, but enforcing total stasis across all civilization for a century is costly and brittle.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abandonment of powerful AI requires flawless coordination and memory for a thousand years despite immense incentives to rebuild; base rate for such renunciations is near zero.

S1.rationale: Coupled extinction requires AI that still needs humans to kill them before achieving self-sufficiency. Rapid AI self-sufficiency makes this narrow despite catastrophic war or bio risks.

S2.rationale: Requires both successful value alignment and later human extinction without continuity. Conjunction of alignment success plus separate extinction is historically unprecedented.

S3.rationale: Indifferent superintelligence pursuing resource or computational goals treats biology as irrelevant. Instrumental convergence makes accidental human elimination the default misalignment outcome.

S4.rationale: If singleton formation is blocked by physics or governance, diverse AIs compete indefinitely for resources and compute. No central winner emerges and humanity is marginalized.

S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion over a millennium guarantees light-speed causal separation. Separated regions will stabilize on different local equilibria from this taxonomy.

S6.rationale: Incentives for brain-computer integration, life extension, and cognitive enhancement are immense and cumulative. Voluntary continuity via uploading or augmentation dissolves the human-AI boundary.

S7.rationale: A singleton superintelligence can cheaply keep humans alive while holding absolute power. Benevolent paternalism or resource fencing both produce this stable stewardship.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal, dynamic balance between separate human and AI powers is game-theoretically unstable. It tends to resolve toward dominance, merger, or fragmentation over centuries.

S9.rationale: Requires human control methods to scale perfectly with capability for a thousand years or permanent capability plateau. Both run counter to observed scaling and incentive trajectories.

S10.rationale: Permanently freezing all change for a century demands perfect prevention of defection and innovation everywhere. Even singleton value-locks erode over interstellar timescales.

S11.rationale: No transformative general-purpose technology has ever been globally and permanently abandoned. Persistent taboo plus perfect enforcement for a millennium has near-zero base rate.
